title: Fixing evening Wi-Fi dropouts caused by channel interference
content:
Applies to: router, broadband.
Typical symptoms: my wifi keeps dropping out every evening around evening; the wireless connection cuts out repeatedly at night but the broadband light on the router stays green.
Cause: Co-channel interference from neighbouring Wi-Fi networks at peak hours on the crowded 2.4 GHz band.
Resolution steps:
1. Confirm the drops only affect Wi-Fi by testing a device on an ethernet cable.
2. Run the router's channel scan and move the 2.4 GHz radio to the least congested channel (1, 6 or 11).
3. Enable the 5 GHz band and connect nearby devices to it.
4. Move the router away from the TV, microwave and metal objects.
5. Update the router firmware to the latest version.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Broadband drops when the phone rings: line noise and microfilters
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: my broadband disconnects whenever the home phone rings; there is crackling on the landline and the internet drops at the same time.
Cause: Electrical noise on the copper line, usually a missing microfilter or a faulty internal extension wiring.
Resolution steps:
1. Fit a microfilter on every phone socket that has a phone or device plugged in.
2. Connect the modem to the master socket using the test socket to bypass internal wiring.
3. Run a remote line test from the support system to check for noise and line faults.
4. If the line test fails, book an engineer visit to repair the line.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Red LOS light on the fibre ONT
content:
Applies to: fiber.
Typical symptoms: my fibre is completely down and the ONT has a red LOS light; no internet at all, the fiber box on the wall shows a red light.
Cause: Loss of optical signal, typically a bent, pinched or disconnected fibre patch lead, or a fault on the network side.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the thin fibre cable into the ONT for sharp bends, kinks or pinching and straighten it.
2. Make sure the green fibre connector is fully clicked into the ONT port without touching the fibre end.
3. Check the outage map for a fibre fault in the area.
4. If LOS stays red, raise a fibre fault and dispatch a field engineer.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Poor indoor mobile coverage and Wi-Fi Calling
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: I have no mobile signal inside my house; calls drop as soon as I walk indoors and the phone shows one bar.
Cause: Weak indoor coverage due to building materials or distance from the mast.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the coverage map for the customer's address.
2. Enable Wi-Fi Calling on the handset so calls route over home broadband.
3. Make sure the phone software and carrier settings are up to date.
4. Offer an indoor signal booster or femtocell if Wi-Fi Calling is not possible.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Device can't join Wi-Fi after a password or security change
content:
Applies to: router.
Typical symptoms: one of my devices won't connect to the wifi after I changed the password; my laptop says incorrect password for the wifi even though it's right.
Cause: Stale saved network profile or the device doesn't support the new security mode (e.g. WPA3-only).
Resolution steps:
1. Forget the saved network on the device and reconnect with the new password.
2. Set the router security mode to WPA2/WPA3 mixed so older devices can join.
3. Check the router's MAC filter or blocked devices list.
4. Update the device's network drivers or firmware.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Connected but no websites load (DNS errors)
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: my internet shows connected but websites won't load; I can't browse any sites although the router says it is online.
Cause: DNS resolution failure: the configured DNS server is unreachable or the local DNS cache is corrupted.
Resolution steps:
1. Confirm the issue is DNS by pinging an IP address such as 8.8.8.8.
2. Flush the DNS cache on the device (ipconfig /flushdns on Windows).
3. Set the router's DNS servers to automatic, or to a public resolver such as 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.
4. Restart the router after changing DNS settings.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Slow broadband at peak evening hours
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: my broadband gets very slow every evening between evening and 11; internet speed drops massively at peak times in the evening.
Cause: Network congestion at peak hours on the local exchange or cabinet backhaul.
Resolution steps:
1. Run a wired speed test at peak and off-peak times to confirm the slowdown is network-side.
2. Check the network capacity dashboard for congestion on the customer's cabinet.
3. Raise a congestion ticket with the network team if utilisation is above threshold.
4. Enable QoS on the router to prioritise video calls during peak hours.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Fibre speed stuck at 100 Mbps: checking cables and router ports
content:
Applies to: fiber, router.
Typical symptoms: I pay for 500 Mbps fibre but only get about 90; my gigabit fiber never goes above 100 Mbps on speed tests.
Cause: A bottleneck in the customer's equipment: a router or ethernet cable limited to 100 Mbps (Fast Ethernet / Cat5).
Resolution steps:
1. Check the negotiated link speed on the computer's network adapter (100 Mbps vs 1 Gbps).
2. Replace old Cat5 ethernet cables with Cat5e or Cat6.
3. Confirm the router has gigabit WAN and LAN ports; replace it with the supported fibre router if not.
4. Re-run a wired speed test directly from the ONT or router.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Phone stuck on 4G with a 5G plan
content:
Applies to: 5g_service, mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: my phone stays on 4G even in 5G areas and data is slow; I have a 5G plan but my phone only shows LTE.
Cause: 5G disabled in handset settings, outdated carrier settings, or an old SIM that is not 5G-provisioned.
Resolution steps:
1. Set the phone's preferred network type to 5G/Auto in mobile network settings.
2. Install the latest carrier settings and phone software update.
3. Check that the SIM is 5G-enabled and replace older SIMs.
4. Confirm 5G is provisioned on the account and the handset model is supported.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Mobile data slowed after reaching the usage allowance
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: my mobile data became extremely slow halfway through the month; data speed dropped to almost nothing after I used a lot this month.
Cause: The plan's fair-usage allowance has been reached and speed is reduced until the next bill cycle.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the data usage against the plan's fair-usage allowance in the account.
2. Explain that speeds are reduced after the allowance until the bill cycle resets.
3. Offer a data add-on or a higher-allowance plan.
4. Set up usage alerts so the customer is notified at 80% of the allowance.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Improving Wi-Fi coverage in distant rooms
content:
Applies to: router.
Typical symptoms: wifi is really slow upstairs but fine next to the router; speeds in the back bedroom are terrible on wifi.
Cause: Insufficient Wi-Fi coverage due to distance, walls or router placement.
Resolution steps:
1. Move the router to a central, elevated, open position rather than a cupboard.
2. Add a mesh Wi-Fi extender or booster disc for distant rooms.
3. Use the 5 GHz band near the router and 2.4 GHz for distant rooms.
4. Run a cable or powerline adapter to the home office for a wired connection.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Handling duplicate payments and refunds
content:
Applies to: billing_system.
Typical symptoms: I have been charged twice for this month's bill; my bank statement shows two identical payments to you.
Cause: A duplicate payment, usually a manual payment plus the scheduled direct debit for the same invoice.
Resolution steps:
1. Verify both transactions in the payments ledger and confirm they are for the same invoice.
2. Raise a refund for the duplicate payment to the original payment method.
3. Tell the customer refunds take 5-7 working days to appear.
4. Offer a goodwill credit if the customer incurred bank charges.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Unrecognised third-party and premium SMS charges
content:
Applies to: billing_system, mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: there are charges for premium text services I never signed up for; my phone bill has third-party subscription charges I don't recognise.
Cause: Third-party premium-rate or direct-carrier-billing subscriptions activated on the line.
Resolution steps:
1. Identify the third-party service and its start date from the billing detail.
2. Cancel the subscription and apply a premium services bar on the line.
3. Raise a refund request for the disputed third-party charges.
4. Advise the customer to enable spending controls for children's phones.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Bill increased after a promotional discount ended
content:
Applies to: billing_system.
Typical symptoms: my bill suddenly went up this month without warning; my monthly price increased a lot and I didn't change anything.
Cause: The introductory promotional discount period ended and the plan reverted to standard price.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the account for an expired promotional discount.
2. Explain that the introductory offer has ended and the plan returned to the standard price.
3. Offer the current retention deals or a cheaper plan that matches usage.
4. Confirm the customer received the end-of-offer notification and note it on the account.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Charged after cancelling a service
content:
Applies to: billing_system.
Typical symptoms: I cancelled my service last month but you're still billing me; I'm still being charged even though I closed my account.
Cause: The cancellation was not processed at the requested date, or a final pro-rata bill was issued.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the cancellation request date and the date the service was actually ceased.
2. If billed past the cancellation date, credit the charges and cancel the direct debit.
3. Explain any legitimate final pro-rata charges or notice-period fees.
4. Confirm the account is closed and send written confirmation.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Early termination fees when moving home
content:
Applies to: billing_system, broadband.
Typical symptoms: I was charged an early termination fee because I moved house; you billed me a cancellation fee when I moved to an area you don't cover.
Cause: Early termination fee applied on cancellation; home-move waivers apply when service is unavailable at the new address.
Resolution steps:
1. Check whether the service is available at the customer's new address.
2. If service is unavailable at the new address, waive the early termination fee under the home-move policy.
3. If service is available, offer to transfer the contract to the new address instead.
4. Issue a corrected final bill.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Router rebooting on its own
content:
Applies to: router.
Typical symptoms: my router keeps rebooting itself several times a day; the router randomly restarts and is very hot to touch.
Cause: Overheating or a failing power supply causing spontaneous reboots.
Resolution steps:
1. Place the router upright in a ventilated spot, not in a cabinet or on other electronics.
2. Check the router's event log for thermal or power-related restarts.
3. Update the router firmware.
4. If reboots continue, replace the router and power adapter.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Modem has no power lights
content:
Applies to: modem.
Typical symptoms: my modem is completely dead with no lights at all; the modem won't turn on, the power light stays off.
Cause: Failed power adapter or modem hardware failure, often after a power surge.
Resolution steps:
1. Confirm the wall socket works and the power adapter is firmly connected.
2. Test with a compatible replacement power adapter if available.
3. If the modem still has no lights, send a replacement modem by next-day delivery.
4. Offer a mobile data hotspot while the replacement is in transit.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: No internet after a router factory reset
content:
Applies to: router, broadband.
Typical symptoms: I factory reset my router and now there's no internet; after pressing the reset button the router connects to wifi but not the internet.
Cause: Factory reset wiped the broadband login (PPPoE username/password) or VLAN settings.
Resolution steps:
1. Log in to the router admin page using the default credentials on the label.
2. Re-enter the broadband PPPoE username and password from the account.
3. Set the WAN VLAN ID required by the network if using a third-party router.
4. Reconfigure the Wi-Fi name and password.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Phone shows 'No SIM' or 'Invalid SIM'
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: my phone says no SIM card inserted; the SIM is not detected and I can't make calls.
Cause: Damaged or worn SIM card, or a SIM tray/reader issue.
Resolution steps:
1. Power off the phone, reseat the SIM in the tray and restart.
2. Test the SIM in another phone to isolate SIM versus handset.
3. If the SIM fails in other phones, issue a replacement SIM and keep the same number.
4. If the SIM works elsewhere, refer the handset for repair.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Router ethernet port not working
content:
Applies to: router.
Typical symptoms: one of the ethernet ports on my router has stopped working; my PC gets no connection when plugged into the router's LAN port.
Cause: Faulty LAN port, damaged cable, or network adapter issue on the computer.
Resolution steps:
1. Try a different LAN port and a known-good ethernet cable.
2. Check the computer's network adapter is enabled and drivers are current.
3. If multiple ports fail, replace the router.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: New fibre installed but not active
content:
Applies to: fiber.
Typical symptoms: the engineer installed my fibre yesterday but there's still no service; my new fiber line was installed but isn't activated.
Cause: Order not yet provisioned on the OLT or ONT serial not registered to the account.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the order status and that the ONT serial number is registered to the account.
2. Trigger provisioning of the service profile on the OLT.
3. Ask the customer to reboot the ONT and router after provisioning.
4. If still not working, escalate to the provisioning team.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: New SIM not activating
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: my new SIM card still isn't active after two days; I got a new SIM but it says emergency calls only.
Cause: Activation pending identity verification (KYC) or the activation step was not completed.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the SIM order status and whether identity verification is pending.
2. Ask the customer to complete identity verification in the app.
3. Manually trigger SIM activation once verification is complete.
4. Ask the customer to restart the phone after activation.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Number porting delayed or failed
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: my number transfer from my old provider is stuck; porting my number has failed and I've got a temporary number.
Cause: Port request rejected or delayed due to a mismatched/expired porting code or account details.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the port request status and any rejection reason.
2. Verify the PAC or porting code is valid, unexpired and matches the number.
3. Resubmit the port request with corrected details.
4. Tell the customer the port completes within one working day of a valid request.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: 5G plan active but 5G not provisioned
content:
Applies to: 5g_service.
Typical symptoms: I switched to the 5G plan but 5G isn't enabled on my line; my plan upgrade to 5G hasn't been activated.
Cause: The 5G service flag was not provisioned on the line after the plan change.
Resolution steps:
1. Check that the 5G service flag is provisioned on the line.
2. Re-provision the 5G service if missing.
3. Ask the customer to restart the handset to refresh network registration.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Speed upgrade not applied
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: I upgraded my broadband package but the speed hasn't changed; I'm paying for the faster plan now but still getting my old speed.
Cause: New speed profile not yet applied to the line, or the router hasn't re-synced to pick it up.
Resolution steps:
1. Confirm the upgrade order is complete and the new speed profile is applied.
2. Ask the customer to restart the router so the line re-syncs at the new profile.
3. Run a line check to confirm the synced speed.
4. If the profile is not applied, escalate to provisioning.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Downgrading a plan during the minimum term
content:
Applies to: billing_system.
Typical symptoms: I want to move to a cheaper plan but was told I can't; how can I downgrade my package to save money.
Cause: Downgrades within the minimum term are restricted; eligibility depends on contract end date.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the contract end date and downgrade eligibility.
2. Explain the downgrade options available now and from the contract end date.
3. Offer usage-matched add-on removal or retention discounts to reduce cost.
4. Schedule the downgrade for the earliest eligible date if the customer agrees.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Adding a line to a family plan
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: I want to add another line to my family plan; how do I add my daughter's phone to my account.
Cause: Customer request to add a line; requires account holder verification and plan eligibility.
Resolution steps:
1. Verify the account holder's identity.
2. Check the plan's maximum lines and shared data options.
3. Add the new line and send a SIM or eSIM.
4. Explain the monthly cost change on the next bill.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Email client settings (IMAP/SMTP)
content:
Applies to: email_service.
Typical symptoms: I can't set up my email account in Outlook; my email stopped sending from my mail app.
Cause: Incorrect IMAP/SMTP server settings, port or authentication.
Resolution steps:
1. Use IMAP server mail.example-telco.com on port 993 with SSL.
2. Use SMTP server smtp.example-telco.com on port 587 with STARTTLS and authentication enabled.
3. Reset the email password from the account portal if authentication keeps failing.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Strict NAT and port forwarding for gaming
content:
Applies to: router.
Typical symptoms: my console says NAT type strict and I can't join online games; I need to open ports on my router for gaming.
Cause: Router NAT restricts inbound connections; UPnP disabled or ports not forwarded.
Resolution steps:
1. Enable UPnP in the router settings.
2. Give the console a reserved IP address in the router DHCP settings.
3. Forward the game's required ports to the console's reserved IP.
4. Restart the console and re-test the NAT type.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Setting up voicemail
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: I can't set up my voicemail; my voicemail isn't working and callers can't leave messages.
Cause: Voicemail not activated, call diversion not set, or PIN unknown.
Resolution steps:
1. Activate voicemail on the line from the account system.
2. Set call diversion on no answer to the voicemail number.
3. Reset the voicemail PIN and send it by SMS.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Requesting a static IP address
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: I need a static IP address for my home server; can I get a fixed IP on my broadband.
Cause: Dynamic public IP allocation; static IP is an add-on.
Resolution steps:
1. Explain the difference between dynamic and static IP addresses.
2. Add the static IP add-on to the account.
3. Ask the customer to restart the router to receive the static IP.
4. Suggest dynamic DNS as a free alternative.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Locked out of the online account
content:
Applies to: account_portal.
Typical symptoms: I'm locked out of my online account; I forgot my password and can't log in.
Cause: Account locked after failed attempts or outdated recovery details.
Resolution steps:
1. Verify the customer's identity with security questions.
2. Unlock the account and send a password reset link.
3. Update the recovery email or mobile number if it is outdated.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: One-time passcode not received
content:
Applies to: account_portal.
Typical symptoms: I'm not receiving the one-time passcode to log in; the OTP verification code never arrives by SMS.
Cause: Outdated mobile number on the account, SMS blocking, or delivery delay.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the mobile number registered for two-factor authentication.
2. Update the number after identity verification if it is outdated.
3. Offer email or authenticator-app verification as an alternative.
4. Check for SMS blocking or spam filtering on the handset.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Changing the account holder
content:
Applies to: account_portal.
Typical symptoms: I need to change the name on the account; how do I transfer the account to my partner.
Cause: Change of account holder request requiring consent or bereavement process.
Resolution steps:
1. Verify the current account holder or the bereavement documentation.
2. Collect the new holder's identity and payment details.
3. Complete the transfer of ownership without interrupting service.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Automatic payment failing
content:
Applies to: billing_system, account_portal.
Typical symptoms: my automatic payment keeps failing; autopay was declined and now I have a late fee.
Cause: Expired or replaced card details on file, or bank mandate cancelled.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the payment failure reason code.
2. Update the card or bank details on the account.
3. Take a one-off payment for the outstanding balance.
4. Waive the late fee as a one-time courtesy if it was the first failure.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Area-wide broadband outage
content:
Applies to: fiber, broadband.
Typical symptoms: the whole neighbourhood has lost internet since this morning; nobody on our street has broadband right now.
Cause: Network outage, e.g. a fibre cable cut by roadworks affecting the area.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the outage map and incident system for the customer's area.
2. Link the customer to the existing incident and share the latest estimated fix time.
3. Offer a mobile data boost or hotspot during the outage.
4. Apply automatic outage compensation once service is restored.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Mobile mast outage in the area
content:
Applies to: mobile_service.
Typical symptoms: there's no mobile service anywhere in town today; my phone and everyone else's has no signal in this area.
Cause: Mobile mast (cell site) outage or maintenance affecting the area.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the network status page for mast outages near the customer's postcode.
2. Share the incident reference and estimated restoration time.
3. Enable Wi-Fi Calling as a workaround if the customer has broadband.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Line damaged by storm
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: after the storm the telephone cable to my house is hanging down; a tree fell on the line and now we have no internet or phone.
Cause: Physical damage to overhead line plant from weather.
Resolution steps:
1. Advise the customer to keep clear of the fallen cable and not touch it.
2. Raise an urgent line damage fault for field repair.
3. Offer a mobile hotspot until the line is repaired.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.

title: Overnight outages from planned maintenance
content:
Applies to: broadband.
Typical symptoms: my internet goes off in the middle of the night for a few hours; the connection was down between midnight and 4am.
Cause: Planned network maintenance windows overnight.
Resolution steps:
1. Check the planned maintenance schedule for the customer's exchange.
2. Confirm the maintenance window and expected completion date.
3. Sign the customer up for maintenance notifications.
If these steps do not resolve the issue, escalate to second-line support with the results of each step.
